The lesson also treats 70% versus 68% as enough to conclude little association without sample-size qualification and ends by claiming completion of all Grade 8 mathematics; both overstatements require clearer, bounded language.

rationale: The residual-gap and sign figures anchor observed-minus-predicted visually, and the sequence then varies direct computation, inverse placement, sign interpretation, a zero case, largest absolute miss, and comparison of two lines at one point. Evaluator targets, sign feedback, hints, equations, and options agree, while the vivid but short explanations remain understandable for Grade 8 and keep the mathematics central.

rationale: The residual-plot figures and curved-data scatter fit contain the right visual foundation, but i1, k1, k2, and the challenge ask learners to infer organized residual shapes from number strings or prose, and the challenge explicitly celebrates working without a picture. Several statements also overclaim that patternless residuals prove the model captured all structure or that the relevant problems are invisible in the scatter plot, while metaphors such as diseases, X-rays, and screaming plots add avoidable language load.
reopenCondition: Reassess after each residual-pattern judgment uses an accessible residual plot, model-diagnostic claims are appropriately qualified, and figurative prose is simplified; reopen on any lesson, course, standards mapping, figure, scatter-fit or choice evaluator, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: This lesson teaches a learner-visible false least-squares result. For points (1,3), (2,6), (3,7), and (4,9), it calls ŷ = 2x + 1 optimal with residuals 0,+1,0,0 and a sum of +1 'essentially balanced'; the actual least-squares line is ŷ = 1.9x + 1.5, whose residuals sum to zero. The visual target, success feedback, k1, trade-off claim, and least-squares explanation therefore disagree with the mathematics, while 'all-zero residuals ... mean the data was invented' is also false and age-inappropriate.
reopenCondition: Release-block until an independent mathematical owner replaces the target line and residual set, aligns evaluator and all feedback with an explicitly stated fit criterion, removes false invented-data language, and verifies the repaired visual at runtime under a new review-basis hash.

The opening concept is nonetheless withheld and names an implicit-circle asset rather than visibly establishing the wall, ladder, x, y, fixed length, and motion arrows, leaving the initial model text-first at the point where a diagram is essential.

rationale: Relation choice, variable classification, cone reduction, and the two-car transfer provide useful variety, but the lesson turns a context-dependent tactic into two absolutes: reduce to one variable before differentiating and never put numbers on a diagram. Its second figure is withheld, the cone and car geometry are text-only, nine expressions have presentation residue, and the generated relation-choice options disclose the answer by length.

rationale: The slope, estimate, concavity-sign, and cube-transfer calculations are correct and the prose is readable for advanced students. The purported tangent-approximation interaction is configured as a continuity/limit verdict, predicts whether two sides approach the same height, and explains jumps rather than comparing a curve with its tangent; the second concept then uses a flat-cubic figure that does not show concave-up or concave-down error direction.

rationale: The lesson moves meaningfully from absolute error to relative error, exponent propagation, roots, and backwards tolerance setting, with correct senior-level explanations. It still has six unstructured π/inequality expressions, the square-root MCQ's correct prose is far longer than its distractors, and its exact-number labs contain no authored exploration states; a cube or uncertainty-band model is preferred so error propagation is seen rather than only calculated.
reopenCondition: Reassess after the shared choices are construction-parallel, every symbolic expression is structured and accessible, and the existing model is verified or enriched with meaningful state exploration; prefer a dimensional uncertainty visual, and reopen on any lesson, course, figure, interaction, renderer, generator, standards-reference, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The secant-to-tangent interaction and corner case are useful, but the lesson states a local leading-order heuristic as an unconditional law: a single value of |f″| at the base point does not by itself determine which of two linearisations is trustworthy over a wider range, because curvature can change across that range. The `dc-linearisation-limits` correct option is also conspicuously longer, and a paired error-versus-distance/curvature graph is preferred over the unrelated flat-cubic opening figure.
reopenCondition: Reassess after error claims are explicitly local and bounded, k2 supplies an interval curvature bound or equivalent hypotheses, option construction is parallel, and preferably a live graph compares distance and curvature effects; reopen on any lesson, course, figure, theorem wording, widget, renderer, generator, standards-reference, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The tangent-ratio figure, removable-hole zoom, valid worked limits, form check, and repeated-application challenge give strong visual and question-job coverage. The opening nevertheless says that two functions vanishing at a make their ratio exactly f′(a)/g′(a), and states L'Hôpital without the needed neighborhood and derivative-limit hypotheses; this is false when the derivative ratio at a is itself undefined or when the theorem's conditions fail, while the generated trap option and three infinity-form strings also have unresolved presentation/parity findings.
reopenCondition: Reassess after the theorem and tangent intuition state sufficient conditions without equating a limit to an unusable pointwise derivative ratio, all forms render accessibly, and generated options pass parity tests; reopen on any lesson, course, theorem, figure, widget, renderer, generator, standards-reference, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The growth hierarchy and the x·ln x calculation are correct, but the lesson overstates that every other indeterminate form can simply be rewritten as a quotient: exponential forms require logarithms, a quotient limit, and exponentiation back, while ∞−∞ does not universally yield merely by taking a common denominator. The same x·ln x example drives k2, the challenge, and remediation; the generic tangent figure does not show any rewrite; eight notation rows and a correct-option length leak remain open.
reopenCondition: Reassess after a visual rewrite map covers product, difference, and exponential forms with full conditions and exponentiation-back, practice uses distinct examples, all notation is structured and accessible, and generated options are parallel; reopen on any lesson, course, figure, theorem wording, widget, renderer, generator, standards-reference, or V4-contract change.

reopenCondition: Reassess after all eight authored notation rows render correctly in concept, feedback, hint, recap, and remedial states; reopen on any lesson, course, renderer, widget, generator, duplicate-reference, standards-reference, or V4-contract change.
